verses.english: Long Discourses 34
Up to Ten
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā campāyaṁ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Campā on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants.

verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

verses.pali: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:
“I will relate the teachings
up to ten for attaining extinguishment,
for making an end of suffering,
the release from all ties.
1. Groups of One

verses.pali: Eko, āvuso, dhammo bahukāro, eko dhammo bhāvetabbo, eko dhammo pariññeyyo, eko dhammo pahātabbo, eko dhammo hānabhāgiyo, eko dhammo visesabhāgiyo, eko dhammo duppaṭivijjho, eko dhammo uppādetabbo, eko dhammo abhiññeyyo, eko dhammo sacchikātabbo.
verses.english: Reverends, one thing is helpful, one thing should be developed, one thing should be completely understood, one thing should be given up, one thing makes things worse, one thing leads to distinction, one thing is hard to comprehend, one thing should be produced, one thing should be directly known, one thing should be realized.
What one thing is helpful?
Diligence in skillful qualities.
What one thing should be developed?
Mindfulness of the body that is full of pleasure.
What one thing should be completely understood?
Contact, which is accompanied by defilements and fuels grasping.
What one thing should be given up?
The conceit ‘I am’.
What one thing makes things worse?
Irrational application of mind.
What one thing leads to distinction?
Rational application of mind.
What one thing is hard to comprehend?
The heart’s immersion of immediate result.
What one thing should be produced?
Unshakable knowledge.
What one thing should be directly known?
All sentient beings are sustained by food.
What one thing should be realized?
The unshakable release of the heart.

verses.pali: Iti ime dasa dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these ten things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
2. Groups of Two

verses.pali: Dve dhammā bahukārā, dve dhammā bhāvetabbā, dve dhammā pariññeyyā, dve dhammā pahātabbā, dve dhammā hānabhāgiyā, dve dhammā visesabhāgiyā, dve dhammā duppaṭivijjhā, dve dhammā uppādetabbā, dve dhammā abhiññeyyā, dve dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Two things are helpful, two things should be developed, two things should be completely understood, two things should be given up, two things make things worse, two things lead to distinction, two things are hard to comprehend, two things should be produced, two things should be directly known, two things should be realized.
What two things are helpful?
Mindfulness and situational awareness.
What two things should be developed?
Serenity and discernment.
What two things should be completely understood?
Name and form.
What two things should be given up?
Ignorance and craving for continued existence.
What two things make things worse?
Being hard to admonish and having bad friends.
What two things lead to distinction?
Being easy to admonish and having good friends.
What two things are hard to comprehend?

verses.pali: Yo ca hetu yo ca paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya, yo ca hetu yo ca paccayo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā.
verses.english: The causes and reasons for the corruption of sentient beings, and the causes and reasons for the purification of sentient beings.
What two things should be produced?
Two knowledges:
knowledge of ending, and knowledge of non-arising.
What two things should be directly known?
Two elements:

verses.pali: saṅkhatā ca dhātu asaṅkhatā ca dhātu.
verses.english: the conditioned element and the unconditioned element.
What two things should be realized?
Knowledge and freedom.

verses.pali: Iti ime vīsati dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these twenty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
3. Groups of Three

verses.pali: Tayo dhammā bahukārā, tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā …pe… tayo dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Three things are helpful, etc.
What three things are helpful?
Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, and practicing in line with the teaching.
What three things should be developed?
Three kinds of immersion.

verses.pali: savitakko savicāro samādhi, avitakko vicāramatto samādhi, avitakko avicāro samādhi.
verses.english: Immersion with placing the mind and keeping it connected. Immersion without placing the mind, merely keeping it connected. Immersion without placing the mind or keeping it connected.
What three things should be completely understood?
Three feelings:

verses.pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā.
verses.english: pleasant, painful, and neutral.
What three things should be given up?
Three cravings:
craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for nonexistence.
What three things make things worse?
Three unskillful roots:

verses.pali: lobho akusalamūlaṁ, doso akusalamūlaṁ, moho akusalamūlaṁ.
verses.english: greed, hate, and delusion.
What three things lead to distinction?
Three skillful roots:

verses.pali: alobho kusalamūlaṁ, adoso kusalamūlaṁ, amoho kusalamūlaṁ.
verses.english: contentment, love, and understanding.
What three things are hard to comprehend?
Three elements of escape.

verses.pali: kāmānametaṁ nissaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ nekkhammaṁ, rūpānametaṁ nissaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ arūpaṁ, yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ, nirodho tassa nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: Renunciation is the escape from sensual pleasures. The formless is the escape from form. Cessation is the escape from whatever is created, conditioned, and dependently originated.
What three things should be produced?
Three knowledges:

verses.pali: atītaṁse ñāṇaṁ, anāgataṁse ñāṇaṁ, paccuppannaṁse ñāṇaṁ.
verses.english: knowledge regarding the past portion, the future portion, and the present portion.
What three things should be directly known?
Three elements:
sensuality, form, and formlessness.
What three things should be realized?
Three knowledges:

verses.pali: pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṁ vijjā, sattānaṁ cutūpapāte ñāṇaṁ vijjā, āsavānaṁ khaye ñāṇaṁ vijjā.
verses.english: recollection of past lives, knowledge of the death and rebirth of sentient beings, and knowledge of the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Iti ime tiṁsa dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these thirty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
4. Groups of Four

verses.pali: Cattāro dhammā bahukārā, cattāro dhammā bhāvetabbā …pe… cattāro dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Four things are helpful, etc.
What four things are helpful?
Four situations:

verses.pali: patirūpadesavāso, sappurisūpanissayo, attasammāpaṇidhi, pubbe ca katapuññatā.
verses.english: living in a suitable region, relying on true persons, being rightly resolved in oneself, and past merit.
What four things should be developed?
The four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: A mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
What four things should be completely understood?
Four foods:

verses.pali: kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṁ catutthaṁ.
verses.english: edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.
What four things should be given up?
Four floods:
sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.
What four things make things worse?
Four yokes:
the yokes of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.
What four things lead to distinction?
Four kinds of unyoking:
unyoking from the yokes of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.
What four things are hard to comprehend?
Four kinds of immersion:

verses.pali: hānabhāgiyo samādhi, ṭhitibhāgiyo samādhi, visesabhāgiyo samādhi, nibbedhabhāgiyo samādhi.
verses.english: immersion liable to decline, stable immersion, immersion that leads to distinction, and immersion that leads to penetration.
What four things should be produced?
Four knowledges:

verses.pali: dhamme ñāṇaṁ, anvaye ñāṇaṁ, pariye ñāṇaṁ, sammutiyā ñāṇaṁ.
verses.english: knowledge of the teaching, inferential knowledge, knowledge of encompassing, and conventional knowledge.
What four things should be directly known?
The four noble truths:

verses.pali: dukkhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ, dukkhasamudayaṁ ariyasaccaṁ, dukkhanirodhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṁ.
verses.english: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.
What four things should be realized?
Four fruits of the ascetic life:
stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

verses.pali: Iti ime cattārīsadhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these forty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
5. Groups of Five

verses.pali: Pañca dhammā bahukārā …pe… pañca dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Five things are helpful, etc.
What five things are helpful?
Five factors that support meditation.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
verses.english: A mendicant has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

verses.pali: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
verses.english: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

verses.pali: Appābādho hoti appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya.
verses.english: They are rarely ill or unwell. Their stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

verses.pali: Asaṭho hoti amāyāvī yathābhūtamattānaṁ āvīkattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu.
verses.english: They’re not devious or deceitful. They reveal themselves honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

verses.pali: Āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
verses.english: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

verses.pali: Paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
verses.english: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
What five things should be developed?
Right immersion with five factors:
pervasion with rapture, pervasion with pleasure, pervasion with mind, pervasion with light, and the basis for reviewing.
What five things should be completely understood?
Five grasping aggregates:
form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
What five things should be given up?
Five hindrances:
sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
What five things make things worse?
Five kinds of hard-heartedness.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.
verses.english: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

verses.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
verses.english: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

verses.pali: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.

verses.english: This is the first kind of hard-heartedness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati …pe…
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has doubts about the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
the training …

verses.pali: sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
verses.english: A mendicant is angry and upset with their spiritual companions, resentful and closed off.

verses.pali: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
verses.english: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.
This is the fifth kind of hard-heartedness.
What five things lead to distinction?
Five faculties:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.
What five things are hard to comprehend?
Five elements of escape.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāme manasikaroto kāmesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: A mendicant focuses on sensual pleasures, but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

verses.pali: Nekkhammaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on renunciation, on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ kāmehi.
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: Ye ca kāmapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi. Na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of sensual pleasures, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from sensual pleasures is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno byāpādaṁ manasikaroto byāpāde cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on ill will, but their mind does not leap forth …

verses.pali: Abyāpādaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto abyāpāde cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on good will, their mind leaps forth …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ byāpādena.
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from ill will.

verses.pali: Ye ca byāpādapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi. Na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ill will, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from ill will is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno vihesaṁ manasikaroto vihesāya cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on harming, but their mind does not leap forth …

verses.pali: Avihesaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto avihesāya cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on compassion, their mind leaps forth …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ vihesāya.
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from harming.

verses.pali: Ye ca vihesāpaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi. Na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of harming, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from harming is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno rūpe manasikaroto rūpesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on form, but their mind does not leap forth …

verses.pali: Arūpaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto arūpe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on the formless, their mind leaps forth …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ rūpehi.
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from forms.

verses.pali: Ye ca rūpapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi. Na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of form, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from forms is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno sakkāyaṁ manasikaroto sakkāye cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on substantial reality, but their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

verses.pali: Sakkāyanirodhaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on the cessation of substantial reality, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ sakkāyena.
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from substantial reality.

verses.pali: Ye ca sakkāyapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi. Na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of substantial reality, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from substantial reality is explained.
What five things should be produced?
Right immersion with five knowledges.

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko’ti paccattaṁyeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.
verses.english: The following knowledges arise for you personally: ‘This immersion is blissful now, and results in bliss in the future.’

verses.pali: ‘Ayaṁ samādhi ariyo nirāmiso’ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.
verses.english: ‘This immersion is noble and not of the flesh.’
‘This immersion is not cultivated by reprobates.’

verses.pali: ‘Ayaṁ samādhi santo paṇīto paṭippassaddhaladdho ekodibhāvādhigato, na sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagato’ti paccattaṁyeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.
verses.english: ‘This immersion is peaceful and sublime and tranquil and unified, not held in place by forceful suppression.’

verses.pali: ‘So kho panāhaṁ imaṁ samādhiṁ satova samāpajjāmi sato vuṭṭhahāmī’ti paccattaṁyeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.
verses.english: ‘I mindfully enter into and emerge from this immersion.’
What five things should be directly known?
Five opportunities for freedom.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṁ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī.
verses.english: Firstly, the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant.

verses.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.
verses.english: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches it.

verses.pali: Tassa atthappaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
verses.english: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.
This is the first opportunity for freedom.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno na heva kho satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī, api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti
verses.english: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant. But the mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.
verses.english: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how they teach it in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Tassa atthappaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
verses.english: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.
This is the second opportunity for freedom.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno na heva kho satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī, nāpi yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti. Api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma. But the mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.
verses.english: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how they rehearse it in detail as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Tassa atthappaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
verses.english: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.
This is the third opportunity for freedom.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno na heva kho satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī, nāpi yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti, nāpi yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma … nor does the mendicant rehearse the teaching.

verses.pali: Api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
verses.english: But the mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.
verses.english: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how they think about and consider it in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Tassa atthappaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
verses.english: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.
This is the fourth opportunity for freedom.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno na heva kho satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī, nāpi yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti, nāpi yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti, nāpi yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati;
verses.english: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma … nor does the mendicant rehearse the teaching … or think about it.

verses.pali: api ca khvassa aññataraṁ samādhinimittaṁ suggahitaṁ hoti sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritaṁ suppaṭividdhaṁ paññāya.
verses.english: But a meditation subject as a basis of immersion is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom.

verses.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhuno aññataraṁ samādhinimittaṁ suggahitaṁ hoti sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritaṁ suppaṭividdhaṁ paññāya tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
verses.english: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how a meditation subject as a basis of immersion is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom.

verses.pali: Tassa atthappaṭisaṁvedino dhammappaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
verses.english: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.
This is the fifth opportunity for freedom.
What five things should be realized?
Five spectrums of the teaching:
ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.

verses.pali: Iti ime paññāsa dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these fifty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
6. Groups of Six

verses.pali: Cha dhammā bahukārā …pe… cha dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Six things are helpful, etc.
What six things are helpful?
Six warm-hearted qualities.

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca,
verses.english: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private.

verses.pali: ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ manokammaṁ …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi, tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī hoti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu, yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni, tathārūpesu sīlesu sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāyaṁ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya, tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhi sāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca,
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who practices it to the complete ending of suffering.

verses.pali: ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo, saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.
What six things should be developed?
Six topics for recollection:

verses.pali: buddhānussati, dhammānussati, saṅghānussati, sīlānussati, cāgānussati, devatānussati.
verses.english: the recollection of the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, ethics, generosity, and the deities.
What six things should be completely understood?
Six interior sense fields:

verses.pali: cakkhāyatanaṁ, sotāyatanaṁ, ghānāyatanaṁ, jivhāyatanaṁ, kāyāyatanaṁ, manāyatanaṁ.
verses.english: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
What six things should be given up?
Six classes of craving:

verses.pali: rūpataṇhā, saddataṇhā, gandhataṇhā, rasataṇhā, phoṭṭhabbataṇhā, dhammataṇhā.
verses.english: craving for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.
What six things make things worse?
Six kinds of disrespect.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso. Dhamme …pe… saṅghe … sikkhāya … appamāde … paṭisanthāre agāravo viharati appatisso.
verses.english: A mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.
What six things lead to distinction?
Six kinds of respect.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari sagāravo viharati sappatisso. Dhamme …pe… saṅghe … sikkhāya … appamāde … paṭisanthāre sagāravo viharati sappatisso.
verses.english: A mendicant has respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.
What six things are hard to comprehend?
Six elements of escape.
Take a mendicant who says:

verses.pali: ‘mettā hi kho me, cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā,
verses.english: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by love. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

verses.pali: atha ca pana me byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
verses.english: Yet somehow ill will still occupies my mind.’

verses.pali: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
verses.english: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

verses.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ āvuso anavakāso yaṁ mettāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya.
verses.english: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the heart’s release by love has been developed and properly implemented,

verses.pali: Atha ca panassa byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
verses.english: yet somehow ill will still occupies the mind.

verses.pali: Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, byāpādassa, yadidaṁ mettācetovimuttī’ti.
verses.english: For it is the heart’s release by love that is the escape from ill will.’
Take another mendicant who says:

verses.pali: ‘karuṇā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.
verses.english: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by compassion. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

verses.pali: Atha ca pana me vihesā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
verses.english: Yet somehow the thought of harming still occupies my mind.’

verses.pali: So: ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo, ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi …pe…
verses.english: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

verses.pali: nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, vihesāya, yadidaṁ karuṇācetovimuttī’ti.
verses.english: For it is the heart’s release by compassion that is the escape from thoughts of harming.’
Take another mendicant who says:
‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by rejoicing. …

verses.pali: atha ca pana me arati cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
verses.english: Yet somehow discontent still occupies my mind.’
They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

verses.pali: nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, aratiyā, yadidaṁ muditācetovimuttī’ti.
verses.english: For it is the heart’s release by rejoicing that is the escape from discontent.’
Take another mendicant who says:
‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by equanimity. …

verses.pali: atha ca pana me rāgo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
verses.english: Yet somehow desire still occupies my mind.’
They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

verses.pali: nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, rāgassa yadidaṁ upekkhācetovimuttī’ti.
verses.english: For it is the heart’s release by equanimity that is the escape from desire.’
Take another mendicant who says:
‘I’ve developed the signless release of the heart. …

verses.pali: atha ca pana me nimittānusāri viññāṇaṁ hotī’ti.
verses.english: Yet somehow my consciousness still follows after signs.’
They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

verses.pali: nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, sabbanimittānaṁ yadidaṁ animittā cetovimuttī’ti.
verses.english: For it is the signless release of the heart that is the escape from all signs.’
Take another mendicant who says:

verses.pali: ‘asmīti kho me vigataṁ, ayamahamasmīti na samanupassāmi,
verses.english: ‘I’m rid of the conceit “I am”. And I don’t regard anything as “I am this”.

verses.pali: atha ca pana me vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
verses.english: Yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupies my mind.’

verses.pali: So: ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
verses.english: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

verses.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ asmīti vigate ayamahamasmīti asamanupassato.
verses.english: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the conceit “I am” has been done away with, and nothing is regarded as “I am this”,

verses.pali: Atha ca panassa vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
verses.english: yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupy the mind.

verses.pali: Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallassa, yadidaṁ asmimānasamugghāto’ti.
verses.english: For it is the uprooting of the conceit “I am” that is the escape from the dart of doubt and indecision.’
What six things should be produced?
Six consistent responses.

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
verses.english: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.
Hearing a sound with their ears …
Smelling an odor with their nose …
Tasting a flavor with their tongue …
Feeling a touch with their body …

verses.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
verses.english: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.
What six things should be directly known?
Six unsurpassable things:

verses.pali: dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ, anussatānuttariyaṁ.
verses.english: the unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.
What six things should be realized?
Six direct knowledges.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhoti—ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṁ tirobhāvaṁ; tirokuṭṭaṁ tiropākāraṁ tiropabbataṁ asajjamāno gacchati seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karoti seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchati seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamati seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parāmasati parimajjati; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vatteti.
verses.english: A mendicant wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

verses.pali: Dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāti dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca.
verses.english: With clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

verses.pali: Parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti,
verses.english: They understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.

verses.pali: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāti …pe…
avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāti.
So anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
verses.english: They recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

verses.pali: Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti …pe…
verses.english: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

verses.pali: Āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life. And they live having realized it with their own insight due to the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Iti ime saṭṭhi dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these sixty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
7. Groups of Seven

verses.pali: Satta dhammā bahukārā …pe… satta dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Seven things are helpful, etc.
What seven things are helpful?
Seven riches of the noble ones:

verses.pali: saddhādhanaṁ, sīladhanaṁ, hiridhanaṁ, ottappadhanaṁ, sutadhanaṁ, cāgadhanaṁ, paññādhanaṁ.
verses.english: the riches of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
What seven things should be developed?
Seven awakening factors:

verses.pali: satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.
verses.english: mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
What seven things should be completely understood?
Seven planes of consciousness.

verses.pali: santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.
This is the first plane of consciousness.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.
This is the second plane of consciousness.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of streaming radiance.
This is the third plane of consciousness.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.
This is the fourth plane of consciousness.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā …pe… ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.
This is the fifth plane of consciousness.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.
This is the sixth plane of consciousness.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.
This is the seventh plane of consciousness.
What seven things should be given up?
Seven underlying tendencies:

verses.pali: kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo, mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo.
verses.english: sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.
What seven things make things worse?
Seven bad qualities:

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, appassuto hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, duppañño hoti.
verses.english: a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, unlearned, lazy, unmindful, and witless.
What seven things lead to distinction?
Seven good qualities:

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, paññavā hoti.
verses.english: a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, energetic, mindful, and wise.
What seven things are hard to comprehend?
Seven aspects of the teachings of the true persons:

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu dhammaññū ca hoti atthaññū ca attaññū ca mattaññū ca kālaññū ca parisaññū ca puggalaññū ca.
verses.english: a mendicant knows the teachings, knows the meaning, knows themselves, knows moderation, knows the right time, knows assemblies, and knows individuals.
What seven things should be produced?
Seven perceptions:

verses.pali: aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, asubhasaññā, ādīnavasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā.
verses.english: the perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of ugliness, the perception of drawbacks, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.
What seven things should be directly known?
Seven qualifications for graduation.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu sikkhāsamādāne tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca sikkhāsamādāne avigatapemo.
verses.english: A mendicant has a keen enthusiasm to undertake the training …

verses.pali: Dhammanisantiyā tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca dhammanisantiyā avigatapemo.
verses.english: to examine the teachings …

verses.pali: Icchāvinaye tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca icchāvinaye avigatapemo.
verses.english: to get rid of desires …

verses.pali: Paṭisallāne tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca paṭisallāne avigatapemo.
verses.english: for retreat …

verses.pali: Vīriyārambhe tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca vīriyārambhe avigatapemo.
verses.english: to rouse up energy …

verses.pali: Satinepakke tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca satinepakke avigatapemo.
verses.english: for mindfulness and alertness …

verses.pali: Diṭṭhipaṭivedhe tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca diṭṭhipaṭivedhe avigatapemo.
verses.english: to penetrate theoretically. And they don’t lose these desires in the future.
What seven things should be realized?
Seven powers of one who has ended the defilements.

verses.pali: idhāvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti.
verses.english: Firstly, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom all conditions as truly impermanent.

verses.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti, idampi khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti: ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.
verses.english: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim: ‘My defilements have ended.’

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom that sensual pleasures are truly like a pit of glowing coals. …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṁ cittaṁ hoti vivekapoṇaṁ vivekapabbhāraṁ vivekaṭṭhaṁ nekkhammābhirataṁ byantībhūtaṁ sabbaso āsavaṭṭhāniyehi dhammehi.
verses.english: Furthermore, the mind of a mendicant with defilements ended slants, slopes, and inclines to seclusion. They’re withdrawn, loving renunciation, and have totally eliminated defiling influences. …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni honti subhāvitāni.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the five faculties. …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the seven awakening factors. …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the noble eightfold path. …

verses.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito, idampi khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
verses.english: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’

verses.pali: Itime sattati dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these seventy things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
The first recitation section is finished.
8. Groups of Eight

verses.pali: Aṭṭha dhammā bahukārā …pe… aṭṭha dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Eight things are helpful, etc.
What eight things are helpful?

verses.pali: Aṭṭha hetū aṭṭha paccayā ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattanti.
verses.english: There are eight causes and reasons that lead to acquiring the wisdom fundamental to the spiritual life, and to its increase, growth, development, and fulfillment once it has been acquired.
What eight?

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthāraṁ upanissāya viharati aññataraṁ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṁ sabrahmacāriṁ, yatthassa tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti pemañca gāravo ca.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant lives relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role. And they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for them, with warmth and respect.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ paṭhamo hetu paṭhamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the first cause.

verses.pali: Taṁ kho pana satthāraṁ upanissāya viharati aññataraṁ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṁ sabrahmacāriṁ, yatthassa tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti pemañca gāravo ca. Te kālena kālaṁ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati paripañhati:
verses.english: When a mendicant lives relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role—with a keen sense of conscience and prudence for them, with warmth and respect—from time to time they go and ask them questions:
‘Why, sir, does it say this?
What does that mean?’

verses.pali: Tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodenti.
verses.english: Those venerables clarify what is unclear, reveal what is obscure, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ dutiyo hetu dutiyo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya, vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the second cause.

verses.pali: Taṁ kho pana dhammaṁ sutvā dvayena vūpakāsena sampādeti—kāyavūpakāsena ca cittavūpakāsena ca.
verses.english: After hearing that teaching they perfect withdrawal of both body and mind.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ tatiyo hetu tatiyo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the third cause.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ catuttho hetu catuttho paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the fourth cause.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ pañcamo hetu pañcamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the fifth cause.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ chaṭṭho hetu chaṭṭho paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the sixth cause.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato. Cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ sattamo hetu sattamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the seventh cause.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu, udayabbayānupassī viharati:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

verses.pali: ‘iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the ending of feeling.

verses.pali: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the ending of perception.

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the ending of choices.

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness.’

verses.pali: Ayaṁ aṭṭhamo hetu aṭṭhamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the eighth cause.
What eight things should be developed?
The noble eightfold path, that is:

verses.pali: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.
verses.english: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
What eight things should be completely understood?
Eight worldly conditions:

verses.pali: lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṁsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañca.
verses.english: gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.
What eight things should be given up?
Eight wrong ways:

verses.pali: micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi.
verses.english: wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.
What eight things make things worse?
Eight grounds for laziness.
Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘kammaṁ kho me kātabbaṁ bhavissati, kammaṁ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilamissati, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I have some work to do. But while doing it my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

verses.pali: So nipajjati, na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
This is the first ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā kammaṁ kataṁ hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho kammaṁ akāsiṁ, kammaṁ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilanto, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I’ve done some work. But while working my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’
They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…
This is the second ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gantabbo hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘maggo kho me gantabbo bhavissati, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilamissati, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I have to go on a journey. But while walking my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’
They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…
This is the third ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gato hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho maggaṁ agamāsiṁ, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilanto, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. But while walking my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’
They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…
This is the fourth ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto na labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, but they didn’t get to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto nālatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo kilanto akammañño, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti …pe…
verses.english: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, but I didn’t get to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is tired and unfit for work. I’d better have a lie down.’…
This is the fifth ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, and they got to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto alatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo garuko akammañño, māsācitaṁ maññe, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, and I got to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is heavy, unfit for work, like I’ve just eaten a load of beans. I’d better have a lie down.’…
They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…
This is the sixth ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno uppanno hoti appamattako ābādho, tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant feels a little sick. They think:

verses.pali: ‘uppanno kho me ayaṁ appamattako ābādho atthi kappo nipajjituṁ, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I feel a little sick. Lying down would be good for me. I’d better have a lie down.’
They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…
This is the seventh ground for laziness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gilānāvuṭṭhito hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has recently recovered from illness.
They think:
‘I’ve recently recovered from illness. My body is weak and unfit for work. I’d better have a lie down.’

verses.pali: Tassa me kāyo dubbalo akammañño, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

verses.english: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…
This is the eighth ground for laziness.
What eight things lead to distinction?
Eight grounds for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhunā kammaṁ kātabbaṁ hoti, tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do. They think:

verses.pali: ‘kammaṁ kho me kātabbaṁ bhavissati, kammaṁ kho pana me karontena na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasikātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘I have some work to do. While working it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

verses.pali: So vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
This is the first ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā kammaṁ kataṁ hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho kammaṁ akāsiṁ, kammaṁ kho panāhaṁ karonto nāsakkhiṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasikātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…
verses.english: ‘I’ve done some work. While I was working I wasn’t able to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’…
This is the second ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gantabbo hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘maggo kho me gantabbo bhavissati, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantena na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasikātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…
verses.english: ‘I have to go on a journey. While walking it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’…
This is the third ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gato hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho maggaṁ agamāsiṁ, maggaṁ kho panāhaṁ gacchanto nāsakkhiṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasikātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…
verses.english: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. While I was walking I wasn’t able to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’…
This is the fourth ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto na labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, but they didn’t get to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto nālatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo lahuko kammañño, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…
verses.english: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, but I didn’t get to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is light and fit for work. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’…
This is the fifth ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, and they got to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto alatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.
verses.english: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, and I got to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is strong and fit for work. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’…

verses.pali: Tassa me kāyo balavā kammañño, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…

verses.english: This is the sixth ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno uppanno hoti appamattako ābādho.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant feels a little sick.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘uppanno kho me ayaṁ appamattako ābādho ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati, yaṁ me ābādho pavaḍḍheyya, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…
verses.english: ‘I feel a little sick. It’s possible this illness will worsen. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’…
This is the seventh ground for arousing energy.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gilānā vuṭṭhito hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has recently recovered from illness.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gilānā vuṭṭhito aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati, yaṁ me ābādho paccudāvatteyya, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘I’ve recently recovered from illness. It’s possible the illness will come back. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

verses.pali: So vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
This is the eighth ground for arousing energy.
What eight things are hard to comprehend?
Eight lost opportunities for spiritual practice.

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, tathāgato ca loke uppanno hoti arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito.
verses.english: Firstly, a Realized One has arisen in the world. He teaches the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One.
But that individual has been reborn in hell.
This is the first lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, tathāgato ca loke uppanno hoti arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito.
verses.english: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.
But that individual has been reborn in the animal realm.
This is the second lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.
But that individual has been reborn in the ghost realm.
This is the third lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.
But that individual has been reborn in one of the long-lived orders of gods.
This is the fourth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

verses.pali: paccantimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti milakkhesu aviññātāresu, yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ upāsakānaṁ upāsikānaṁ.
verses.english: But that individual has been reborn in the borderlands, among uneducated foreigners, where monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen do not go.
This is the fifth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

verses.pali: ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti micchādiṭṭhiko viparītadassano:
verses.english: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they have wrong view and distorted perspective:

verses.pali: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ, natthi hutaṁ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, natthi ayaṁ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
verses.english: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’
This is the sixth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

verses.pali: ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti duppañño jaḷo eḷamūgo, nappaṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṁ.
verses.english: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they’re witless, dull, idiotic, and unable to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.
This is the seventh lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
Furthermore, no Realized One has arisen in the world,

verses.pali: ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti paññavā ajaḷo aneḷamūgo, paṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṁ.
verses.english: so there is no teaching of the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One. But an individual is reborn in a central country. And they’re wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.
This is the eighth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.
What eight things should be produced?
Eight thoughts of a great man.
‘This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.
It’s for the contented, not those who lack contentment.
It’s for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.
It’s for the energetic, not the lazy.
It’s for the mindful, not the unmindful.
It’s for those with immersion, not those without immersion.

verses.pali: Paññavato ayaṁ dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo duppaññassa.
verses.english: It’s for the wise, not the witless.

verses.pali: Nippapañcassāyaṁ dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo papañcārāmassāti ime aṭṭha dhammā uppādetabbā.
verses.english: This teaching is for those who don’t enjoy proliferating, not for those who enjoy proliferating.’
What eight things should be directly known?
Eight dimensions of mastery.

verses.pali: ajjhattaṁ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—
verses.english: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the first dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—
verses.english: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the second dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—
verses.english: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the third dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—
verses.english: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni.
verses.english: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṁ nīlaṁ nīlavaṇṇaṁ nīlanidassanaṁ nīlanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ nīlaṁ nīlavaṇṇaṁ nīlanidassanaṁ nīlanibhāsaṁ;
verses.english: They’re like a flax flower that’s blue, with blue color and blue appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

verses.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.
verses.english: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni.
verses.english: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṁ pītaṁ pītavaṇṇaṁ pītanidassanaṁ pītanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ pītaṁ pītavaṇṇaṁ pītanidassanaṁ pītanibhāsaṁ;
verses.english: They’re like a champak flower that’s yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

verses.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.
verses.english: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni.
verses.english: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are red, with red color and red appearance.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṁ lohitakaṁ lohitakavaṇṇaṁ lohitakanidassanaṁ lohitakanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ lohitakaṁ lohitakavaṇṇaṁ lohitakanidassanaṁ lohitakanibhāsaṁ;
verses.english: They’re like a scarlet mallow flower that’s red, with red color and red appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, red, with red color and red appearance.

verses.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.
verses.english: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the seventh dimension of mastery.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni.
verses.english: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are white, with white color and white appearance.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ odātaṁ odātavaṇṇaṁ odātanidassanaṁ odātanibhāsaṁ;
verses.english: They’re like the morning star that’s white, with white color and white appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, white, with white color and white appearance.

verses.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.
verses.english: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’
This is the eighth dimension of mastery.
What eight things should be realized?
Eight liberations.
Having physical form, they see forms.
This is the first liberation.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati.
verses.english: Not perceiving physical form internally, someone see forms externally.
This is the second liberation.
They’re focused only on beauty.
This is the third liberation.

verses.pali: Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.
This is the fourth liberation.

verses.pali: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.
This is the fifth liberation.

verses.pali: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.
This is the sixth liberation.

verses.pali: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.
This is the seventh liberation.

verses.pali: Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.
This is the eighth liberation.

verses.pali: Iti ime asīti dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.
verses.english: So these eighty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.
9. Groups of Nine

verses.pali: Nava dhammā bahukārā …pe… nava dhammā sacchikātabbā.
verses.english: Nine things are helpful, etc.
What nine things are helpful?

verses.pali: Nava yonisomanasikāramūlakā dhammā, yonisomanasikaroto pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati, samāhite citte yathābhūtaṁ jānāti passati, yathābhūtaṁ jānaṁ passaṁ nibbindati, nibbindaṁ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati.
verses.english: Nine things rooted in rational application of mind. When you apply the mind rationally, joy springs up. When you’re joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, you feel bliss. And when you’re blissful, the mind becomes immersed. When your mind is immersed, you truly know and see. When you truly know and see, you grow disillusioned. Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away you’re freed.
What nine things should be developed?
Nine factors of trying to be pure.

verses.pali: sīlavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, cittavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, diṭṭhivisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, paññāvisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, vimuttivisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ.
verses.english: The factors of trying to be pure in ethics, mind, view, overcoming doubt, knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path, knowledge and vision of the practice, knowledge and vision, wisdom, and freedom.
What nine things should be completely understood?
Nine abodes of sentient beings.

verses.pali: santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.
verses.english: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.
This is the first abode of sentient beings.

verses.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.
